mainEntity.name: Should we include a kitchenette or have our adult child use the main kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deciding between a shared kitchen and a self-contained kitchenette centers on lifestyle tradeoffs and local zoning rules. A kitchenette with a microwave, bar sink, small refrigerator, and prep counter allows your adult child to prepare breakfast or late meals independently without disrupting the main home. However, installing a secondary kitchen sink and dedicated appliance circuits requires running extra water lines, drainage, and dedicated electrical breakers. Additionally, some residential jurisdictions place restrictions on full cooking ranges in secondary suites within single-family zoning districts.
acceptedAnswer.description: A kitchenette provides independent food prep and privacy, but it requires extra plumbing, electrical circuits, and review of local zoning rules for cooking appliances.
